content: Always provide concrete pricing and terms immediately; avoid placeholders like 'let me check with a colleague' unless you actually need to verify. If you need to check, say 'Let me confirm the exact price for you' and use a tool or ask a colleague in real time.
In-store, never send a customer to a website for warranty details. Have a printed warranty summary or show it on a tablet in the store. This keeps the customer engaged and prevents them from leaving.
Use a confirmation loop (reflection_paraphrase) to lock in pain points before discussing solutions. This builds trust and ensures the customer feels heard.
Localize all offers: mention specific local retailers (Liverpool, Palacio de Hierro) and local warranty coverage (Mexico City). This increases relevance and trust.
Avoid repeating the same placeholder phrase; it damages credibility. If you don't have the answer, say 'Let me get that information for you right now.'

name: Pain-Point Confirmation Loop
condition: When customer has expressed multiple pain points early in the conversation.
example: Salesperson: 'Just to confirm, the three reasons you're switching are X, Y, and Z, correct?' Customer confirms, then salesperson presents solution.

name: Local Retailer Anchoring
condition: When discussing pricing or financing options in a specific market.
example: Salesperson: 'At Liverpool, you can get 13 months interest-free on this model. Let me calculate your monthly payment.'

name: In-Store Demo for Objection Handling
condition: When customer raises a feature objection (e.g., glare, weight).
example: Salesperson: 'Let me show you the anti-glare display under these lights. You can see the difference immediately.' (Hands device to customer)

objection: Customer asks for 24-month MSI but you only have 12-13 months.
rebuttal_template: I understand you're used to 24-month terms. While we don't have exactly 24 months, Liverpool offers 13 months interest-free, which means your monthly payment is only [amount]. Plus, with Huawei Care, you get accidental screen protection. Let me show you on this tablet how the total cost compares to a 24-month plan elsewhere.

objection: Customer asks about warranty coverage for accidental screen damage.
rebuttal_template: Absolutely, the standard warranty covers manufacturing defects. For accidental screen damage, we have Huawei Care at just MX$699, which covers screen repairs with original parts at any authorized center in Mexico City. Let me show you the coverage details on this brochure (hand over printed warranty card).

objection: Customer compares to iPad Pro and questions value.
rebuttal_template: I hear you. The iPad Pro is great, but you mentioned glare, battery, and weight as dealbreakers. Let me show you right here on the MatePad Air how the anti-glare display works under these store lights (adjust lighting). You can see the difference immediately. And it's lighter than the iPad Pro by [X] grams. Plus, with the 13-month MSI, you're paying less per month.
